newsitem.title: USA: Business confidence rises in the first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Business confidence rises in the first quarter.

text.p: Confidence among top executives continued to rise in the first quarter, according to a recent survey of chief executive officers.
The index, the quarterly Measure of Business Confidence survey taken by the Conference Board, rose to 57 in the first quarter, the highest level since the third quarter of 1994, when it measured 59.
The index was up from 54 in the fourth quarter of 1996 and 53 in the third quarter, the business research group said.
A reading above 50 reflects more positive than negative responses from business leaders, according to the firm.

"We began 1997 with healthy job growth, and this pace is expected to accelerate in the coming months," said Lynn Franco, assciate director of the Conference Board's Consumer Reserach Centre in a statement.

Forty-seven percent of the more than 150 chief executive officers surveyed said the economy has improved over the last six months, up from less than 45 percent in the prior quarter. More than 45 percent said they were "marginally" more positive about business conditions in their own industries, while those reporting worse conditions fell to 16 percent, the Conference Board said.
Among industries, CEOs in wholesale and retail trade reported the largest improvement in business conditions. Banking and finance deteriorated.

The report also noted that more than 30 percent of executives plan to hire additional workers during the upcoming year, up significantly from the 10 percent figure seen a year ago. About 10 percent said they would decrease their workforce, down from 45 percent a year ago.
CEOs said wage and salary costs and other benefits are not major obstacles to hiring more workers. Regulations and litigation, and health care costs were cited as the largest hiring obstacles.
The conference board is a private business research and membership network.
